rationale: Tests the foundational pathophysiological distinction between asthma and COPD — the block that establishes why drug selection diverges between the two conditions.
Tests the high-stakes LABA monotherapy safety distinction between asthma and COPD — the single most important drug safety fact in the beta-2 agonist section.

Tests application of leukotriene modifier pharmacology to aspirin-exacerbated asthma with co-existing rhinitis — integrating drug mechanism, indication, and dual-disease management from the anti-inflammatory agents block.

Tests the common misconception that oral antihistamines are the most effective monotherapy for allergic rhinitis — the rhinitis block establishes intranasal corticosteroids as the superior single drug class.

Tests clinical decision-making in asthma management during pregnancy — the clinical decision-making block establishes that uncontrolled asthma poses greater foetal risk than continued inhaled therapy.
Tests recall of the cough reflex arc sequence — understanding where each drug class acts requires knowing the order of the sensory, integrative, and motor components described in this block.
Tests the critical drug interaction between dextromethorphan and MAOIs — the antitussive section establishes this as an absolute contraindication with life-threatening consequences.
Tests the fundamental cough-type-determines-drug-class principle — the expectorants and mucolytics block establishes that productive cough requires mucolytics, never antitussives.

Tests age-specific prescribing considerations for cough in young children — the clinical decision-making block establishes that codeine is contraindicated under 12 and honey is the evidence-based first-line for children over 1 year.
